s_recommended_selections_note: Recommended selections are for normal users and if you are unsure do NOT check anything else!
s_choose_official_iso: Choose an official Windows 11 ISO downloaded from Microsoft. It will be mounted and checked before anything is changed.
s_third_party_images: Third-party, pre-modified, or unofficial images are not supported and may produce broken results. This is only meant for fresh and new Windows installs.
s_download_page_choice: On the download page choose Windows 11, your language, and 64-bit (x64).
s_pick_what_goes_into_image: Pick what goes into the image, then start. This takes several minutes depending on your hardware.
s_save_modified_image: Save the modified image as an ISO file, or write it straight to a USB drive you can boot from.
s_usb_erase_warning: !! All data on the selected USB drive will be permanently erased !!
s_note_appx_packages: Note: Select the Windows AppX packages you wish to install or remove.
s_appx_install_note: 'Install Selected' registers a local manifest for the current user when available, then falls back to the Microsoft Store.
s_appx_remove_note: 'Remove Selected' removes packages for all users and stops new profiles from getting them by default.
s_guide_updates_benefits:
Applies a consistent update policy in one step.
Keep current makes no change at all.
s_guide_install_info: Nothing is installed until you press Apply all in order on the review screen.
s_guide_config_info: Only a small, well-understood set of features is enabled here. Use the Advanced Config tab for anything else.
s_guide_tweaks_warning: Advanced includes changes that may need a restart or sign-out.
s_guide_updates_desc: Windows Update can be left as it is, restored to defaults, set to recommended values, or disabled.
s_guide_updates_warning: Disabling Windows Update is not recommended: your machine stops receiving security fixes.
s_guide_appx_info: You can restore most of these apps from the Microsoft Store later.
s_guide_restorepoint_desc: Windows can take a snapshot of your system settings before anything changes. If something does not behave as expected, you can roll back to this point.
s_guide_restorepoint_info: Recommended on a fresh install. WinUtil still finishes the remaining steps if you choose No.
s_guide_tweaks_desc: Presets are curated groups of Windows tweaks. Pick the level that matches how much you want to change.
s_guide_install_desc: Pick the applications you want on this machine. WinUtil installs them with your preferred package manager and upgrades the ones that already have a newer version.
s_guide_config_benefits: Older applications and installers run without missing-runtime errors.
s_guide_tweaks_changes:
Standard: balanced defaults for most users.
Minimal: only the safest, least invasive tweaks.
Advanced: deeper changes for power users.
s_guide_appx_warning: On a portable device this also removes built-in utilities you may rely on.
s_guide_tweaks_info: Choosing None leaves your current tweaks untouched.
s_guide_review_info: Skipped steps are listed in the summary and are not applied.
s_guide_restorepoint_benefits:
Gives you a rollback point before tweaks and features are applied.
Takes only a few seconds and needs no restart.
s_guide_review_benefits:
One click runs everything in order.
Jobs are queued, so nothing runs at the same time.
s_guide_review_changes: Restore point (if chosen), then tweaks, apps, features, AppX, and finally updates.
s_guide_config_desc: Adds the .NET Framework versions that many older Windows applications still depend on.
s_guide_appx_benefits:
A cleaner Start menu.
Less background activity from apps you do not use.
s_guide_install_changes:
Downloads and installs the selected applications.
Upgrades applications that already have a newer version available.
s_guide_appx_desc: Removes the pre-installed consumer apps that are usually not needed on a fresh Windows install.
s_guide_updates_changes:
Recommended: defers feature updates and configures download-and-notify.
Defaults: restores the Windows Update policies and services.
Disable: turns off Windows Update and its services.
s_guide_review_desc: Check what you selected. Press Apply all in order to run the actions in the safest order.
s_guide_tweaks_benefits:
No need to review every tweak individually.
You can undo the applied tweaks later from the Tweaks tab.
s_guide_config_changes:
Enables .NET Framework 4 Advanced Services and .NET Framework 3.5.
May require a restart to finish.
s_guide_install_benefits:
One pass for all your apps.
Uses winget or Chocolatey according to your preference.
s_guide_restorepoint_changes:
Creates a restore point through Windows System Protection.
Does not change applications, files, or personal settings.
s_guide_appx_changes:
Removes the AppxDefault set of packaged apps for all users.
Stops those apps from being provisioned for new profiles.
s_guide_updates_info: Disable Updates asks for confirmation before it runs.
s_tweak_DisableStoreSearch: Microsoft Store Recommended Search Results - Disable
s_tweak_UTC: Date & Time - Set Time to UTC
s_tweak_RemoveHomeAndGallery: File Explorer Home and Gallery - Disable
s_tweak_Display: Visual Effects - Set to Best Performance
s_tweak_EndTaskOnTaskbar: End Task With Right Click - Enable
s_tweak_DisableExplorerAutoDiscovery: File Explorer Automatic Folder Discovery - Disable
s_desc_Activity: Stops Windows from publishing or uploading user activities while preserving clipboard history.
s_desc_Hiber: Hibernation is really meant for laptops as it saves what's in memory before turning the PC off. It really should never be used.
s_desc_Widget: Removes the annoying widgets in the bottom left of the Taskbar.
s_desc_RevertStartMenu: Bring back the old Start Menu layout from before the gradual rollout of the new one in 25H2. On newer versions of Windows !!THIS TWEAK WILL NOT WORK!!
s_desc_DisableStoreSearch: Will not display recommended Microsoft Store apps when searching for apps in the Start menu.
s_desc_Services: Sets some services to Manual startup.
s_desc_SvcHostSplitting: Disables service-host splitting to reduce the number of svchost.exe processes and modestly lower memory overhead. Recommended for low-performance systems with 12 GB of RAM or less. Can interfere with Xbox services. Restart Windows after changing this setting.
s_desc_BraveDebloat: Disables various annoyances like Brave Rewards, Leo AI, Crypto Wallet and VPN.
s_desc_DisableWarningForUnsignedRdp: Disables warnings shown when launching unsigned RDP files introduced with the latest Windows 10 and 11 updates.
s_desc_EdgeDebloat: Disables various telemetry options, popups, and other annoyances in Edge.
s_desc_ConsumerFeatures: Stops promoted app installs and reduces app suggestions from Microsoft Store content.
s_desc_DeliveryOptimization: Stops Windows from using your bandwidth to upload updates to other PCs on the internet or local network.
s_desc_RemoveEdge: Uninstalls Microsoft Edge by creating dummy MicrosoftEdge.exe file in the legacy Edge folder. This tricks Windows into unlocking the official Edge uninstaller allowing for a system-level removal.
s_desc_UTC: Essential for computers that are dual booting. Fixes the time sync with Linux systems.
s_desc_RemoveOneDrive: Denies permission to remove OneDrive user files, then uses its own uninstaller to remove it and restores the original permission afterward.
s_desc_RemoveHomeAndGallery: Removes the Home and Gallery from Explorer and sets This PC as default.
s_desc_Display: Sets the system preferences to performance. You can do this manually with sysdm.cpl as well.
s_desc_ReservedStorage: Disables Windows Reserved Storage (7-10 GB held for updates/temp files). Recommended only on small drives. Re-enable before major Windows feature updates to avoid installation failures.
s_desc_RestorePoint: Creates a restore point at runtime in case a revert is needed from WinUtil modifications.
s_desc_EndTaskOnTaskbar: Enables option to end task when right-clicking a program in the taskbar.
s_desc_Storage: Storage Sense deletes temp files automatically.
s_desc_WindowsAI: Removes and disables all AI features/packages
s_desc_WPBT: If enabled, WPBT allows your computer vendor to execute programs at boot time, such as anti-theft software, software drivers, as well as force install software without user consent. Poses potential security risk.
s_desc_PreventDeviceMetadataFromNetwork: Prevents additional software from being installed when plugging in devices (e.g. Ads when plugging in a monitor). Poses potential security risk.
s_desc_RazerBlock: Blocks ALL Razer Software installations. The hardware works fine without any software.
s_desc_LogiBlock: Blocks the Logi Download Assistant that Windows Update keeps reinstalling with Logitech device drivers. Logitech hardware keeps working without it.
s_desc_BlockAdobeNet: Reduces user interruptions by selectively blocking connections to Adobe's activation and telemetry servers. Credit: Ruddernation-Designs
s_desc_RightClickMenu: Restores the classic context menu when right-clicking in File Explorer, replacing the simplified Windows 11 version.
s_desc_DiskCleanup: Runs Disk Cleanup on Drive C: and removes old Windows Updates.
s_desc_IPv46: Setting the IPv4 preference can have latency and security benefits on private networks where IPv6 is not configured.
s_desc_Teredo: Teredo network tunneling is an IPv6 feature that can cause additional latency, but may cause problems with some games.
s_desc_DisableSearchIndexing: Stops and disables the Windows Search service (WSearch) to cut background disk activity, mainly useful on mechanical hard drives. Warning: file searches in Explorer and the Start menu become much slower because Windows no longer maintains a search index. Undo restores the service and starts it again.
s_desc_DisableBGapps: Disables all Microsoft Store apps from running in the background, which has to be done individually since Windows 11.
s_desc_DisableExplorerAutoDiscovery: Windows Explorer automatically tries to guess the type of the folder based on its contents, slowing down the browsing experience. WARNING! Will disable File Explorer grouping.
s_desc_WPFToggleDetailedBSoD: Gives more information when you blue screen.
s_desc_WPFToggleBatteryPercentage: Shows numeric battery percentage next to the battery icon in the system tray.
s_desc_WPFToggleDarkMode: Dark Mode for the system and applications.
s_desc_WPFToggleNewOutlook: This will ensure the new Outlook application is used.
s_desc_WPFToggleScrollbars: If enabled, scrollbars will always be visible. If disabled, Windows will automatically hide scrollbars when not in use.
s_desc_WPFMultiplaneOverlay: Multiplane Overlay composes multiple image layers, which can sometimes cause issues with graphics cards. Changes to this preference are applied immediately.
s_desc_WPFToggleMouseAcceleration: Makes it so Cursor movement is affected by the speed of your physical mouse movements.
s_desc_WPFToggleNumLock: Toggle the Num Lock key state when your computer starts.
s_desc_WPFToggleWindowSnapping: Toggles the window snapping feature when dragging windows.
s_desc_WPFToggleStandbyFix: Toggles network connectivity during S0 Sleep which is low power idle in modern laptops.
s_desc_WPFToggleS3Sleep: Toggles between Modern Standby and S3 Sleep, which cuts off power to the CPU while continuing to refresh the memory.
s_desc_WPFToggleHideSettingsHome: Toggles the Home Page in the Windows Settings app.
s_desc_WPFToggleBingSearch: Toggles Bing web search results in Windows Search.
s_desc_WPFToggleLoginBlur: Toggles the acrylic blur effect on login screen background.
s_desc_WPFToggleDisableLockscreen: Skips the lock screen entirely and goes directly to the sign-in screen on boot and wake.
s_desc_WPFToggleStartMenuRecommendations: Toggles the recommendations section in the Start Menu. WARNING: This will also disable Windows Spotlight on your Lock Screen as a side effect.
s_desc_WPFToggleStickyKeys: Toggles the Sticky Keys, which activate when clicking shift rapidly.
s_desc_WPFToggleTaskbarAlignment: Toggles the Taskbar alignment either to the left or center.
s_desc_WPFToggleTaskbarSearch: Toggles the Search Button on the Taskbar.
s_desc_WPFToggleTaskView: Toggles the Task View Button in the Taskbar.
s_desc_WPFToggleGameMode: Toggles Windows prioritizes gaming performance by allocating system resources to games.
s_desc_WPFToggleLongPaths: Toggles support for file paths longer than 260 characters in Explorer.
s_desc_WPFOOSUbutton: Downloads O&O ShutUp10++ (about 82 MB) from oo-software.com on every click and launches it. Nothing is installed; the file is saved under %LocalAppData%\winutil.
s_desc_sdotnet: .NET and .NET Framework is a developer platform made up of tools, programming languages, and libraries for building many different types of applications.
s_desc_WPFFixesNTPPool: Replaces the default Windows NTP server (time.windows.com) with pool.ntp.org for improved time synchronization accuracy and reliability.
s_desc_shyperv: Hyper-V is a hardware virtualization product developed by Microsoft that allows users to create and manage virtual machines.
s_desc_slegacymedia: Enables legacy programs from previous versions of Windows.
s_desc_wsl: Windows Subsystem for Linux is an optional feature of Windows that allows Linux programs to run natively on Windows without the need for a separate virtual machine or dual booting.
s_desc_nfs: Network File System (NFS) is a mechanism for storing files on a network.
s_desc_RegBackup: Enables daily registry backup, previously disabled by Microsoft in Windows 10 1803.
s_desc_EnableLegacyRecovery: Enables Advanced Boot Options screen that lets you start Windows in advanced troubleshooting modes.
s_desc_DisableLegacyRecovery: Disables Advanced Boot Options screen that lets you start Windows in advanced troubleshooting modes.
s_desc_sSandbox: Windows Sandbox is a lightweight virtual machine that provides a temporary desktop environment to safely run applications and programs in isolation.
s_appnav_desc_WPFInstall: Install or upgrade the selected applications
s_appnav_desc_WPFInstallUpgrade: Upgrade all applications to the latest version
s_appnav_desc_WPFInstallFOSSInfo: Information about the #FOSS label on application entries
